   79: ## Required change 3: rollback â€” bounded quiescence wait + epoch fence for residual messages
   80: 
   81: Two independent fixes, since Codex correctly separated "did admitted invocations finish" from "is
   82: replaying old residual work semantically valid":
   83: 
   84: **Quiescence**: Rollback Apply A (disable both mappings) is followed by an explicit wait of
   85: `max(scanLambdaTimeout, claimLambdaTimeout) = 90s` (round 3's scan Lambda timeout, still the
   86: larger of the two) before Rollback Apply B may proceed â€” long enough that ANY invocation admitted
   87: in the instant before the mapping was disabled has either completed or been killed by its own
   88: Lambda timeout; this is a NAMED, bounded wait (not "monitoring, non-blocking" as round 4 wrongly
   89: called it), stated as a concrete runbook step with a concrete number, not an operator's judgment
   90: call.
   91: 
   92: **Epoch fence** (answers Codex's deeper point â€” a quiesced system can still hold OLD, valid-looking
   93: messages whose replay is semantically stale): every start/continuation event's `data` gains one
   94: more field, `rolloutEpoch` (an integer, incremented each time `SCAN_MODE` flips `LEGACY`â†’`PAGED`,
   95: stored as a Lambda environment variable alongside `SCAN_MODE` itself, e.g.
   96: `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH="2"`). The scan handler, on receiving ANY message (start or continuation),
   97: compares the message's `rolloutEpoch` against its OWN environment's current `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH`; a
   98: mismatch (message from a PRIOR epoch â€” i.e., queued before the last rollback/roll-forward cycle) is
   99: treated as a stale no-op, ack'd and dropped, logged `"stale epoch, dropped"` with a
  100: dedicated metric (`StaleEpochMessageDropped`, Count) so an operator can see this happening rather
  101: than have it silently vanish. This makes "leave residual messages queued for a future re-enable"
  102: actually safe by construction (Codex's exact objection) â€” a future re-enable bumps the epoch again,
  103: so anything left over from BEFORE the rollback is automatically invalidated rather than assumed
  104: valid via idempotency alone. Claim-candidate messages do NOT need this fence (they're not part of
  105: the lease chain â€” a stale candidate simply attempts its normal conditional claim, which is either
  106: still valid, in which case claiming it late is correct behavior no different from claiming it on
  107: time, or already resolved, in which case the existing not-found/lost-race no-op paths handle it â€”
  108: no new field needed there, kept as-is from round 4).

  885: Arquivos de transcript bruto (`.txt`, prefixo `_`, ou os `full-audit-*-codex-output-*.txt`) nunca sÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â£o fonte de verdade por si sÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â³ ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â sempre prefira o `.md` de resumo/nota que os acompanha. **PolÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â­tica de proveniÃƒÆ’Ã‚Âªncia/metadata**: os `.md` de nota/resumo carregam frontmatter (`status`/`owner`/`authority`, mais `Last verified` nos routers); os `.txt` brutos nÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â£o ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â exigir frontmatter em cada transcript violaria proporcionalidade (`principles.md` #1) sem ganho real, jÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¡ que sua proveniÃƒÆ’Ã‚Âªncia ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â© herdada do `.md` que os acompanha (mesmo prefixo de nome) e da posiÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â§ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â£o cronolÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â³gica descrita nesta seÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â§ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â£o.   906: from round 1/2 NOT contradicted here stands unchanged (names in round-1 Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§1, error taxonomy
  907: conclusion that no new `AppError` subclass is needed, most of round-2's port/schema-file-location
  908: corrections). This round's central fix: **the checkpoint-before-continuation ordering bug (required
  909: changes 1+2) is resolved by using this codebase's OWN transactional outbox pattern for the
  910: checkpoint transition** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â the same mechanism `producer.ts:264-306` already uses for
  911: claimÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢dispatch, applied one layer up, to scan-pageÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢continuation. Round 2's own "outbox doesn't
  912: apply here, there's no aggregate write" reasoning (round 1 Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§4) was the actual mistake: **the lease

  915: ## Required changes 1+2: checkpoint/continuation ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â outbox-atomic, not send-then-checkpoint
  916: 
  917: **`SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` is reinstated in `OutboxDestination`** (round 2 wrongly
  918: removed it). Checkpoint transition (after a page's candidates are durably published, see Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§7 below)
  919: is now ONE `TransactWriteItems`, same shape as `producer.ts:286-306`:
  920: ```ts
  921: const outboxEntries: DynamoTransactPutEntry[] = [];
  922: appendToTransaction(outboxEntries, deps.tableName, continuationEvent, "SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1");
  923: await deps.store.transactWrite([
  924:   { Update: buildUnscopedVersionedUpdate({ tableName, key: leaseKey, expectedVersion: leaseVersionThisInvocationRead, set: { lastEvaluatedKey: nextKey /* or REMOVE + status: "COMPLETED" on last page */, leaseUntil: now + LEASE_MS, pagesProcessed: pagesProcessed + 1, candidatesPublished: candidatesPublished + thisPageCount }, extraConditions: [{ expression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND #startKeyCond", ... }] }) },
  925:   ...outboxEntries,
  926: ]);
  927: ```
  928: `DispatchOutboxRelay` (DynamoDB Streams, `producer.ts:270`'s existing mechanism) is extended to
  929: also recognize `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` and publish to the scan queue instead of the
  930: dispatch queue ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â same relay, same sweeper-recovers-publish-failures guarantee, routed by the
  931: existing `destination` discriminator (no new relay Lambda). **Verified this round, not just
  932: asserted**: `src/workers/dispatch-outbox-relay/relay.ts:12-14,22-27,122-152` shows the relay is
  933: ALREADY a generalized multi-destination router (`senders: Record<OutboxDestination, Sender>`,
  934: one sweeper instance covers multiple destinations) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â it already recognizes
  935: `SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1` and `SQS_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_V1` side by side, so adding a third
  936: `senders` entry for `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` (pointing at the scan queue URL) is the
  937: exact, already-precedented extension point ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â no relay redesign needed. **This closes required change 1's
  938: exact failure trace**: a continuation now literally cannot exist in SQS until the checkpoint
  939: transaction has committed, so "successor consumed before predecessor checkpoint" is impossible by
  940: construction ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â there is no window where a successor can arrive early, because the successor's own
  941: existence is downstream of (caused by) the checkpoint, not concurrent with it. Required change 2's
  942: "specify a rigorous successor protocol" is answered by removing the need for one: at-least-once
  943: delivery of the SAME continuation (streams relay redelivery, sweeper retry, or SQS standard-queue
  944: redelivery) is idempotent because the checkpoint that produced it already advanced
  945: `lastEvaluatedKey` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a redelivered continuation's handler re-reads the CURRENT lease row, finds
  946: `lastEvaluatedKey` already matches (or is already past) what the message describes as "next to
  947: process," and either does the work once (first delivery) or no-ops (subsequent redeliveries,
  948: detected by comparing the message's OWN `lastEvaluatedKey` against the row's, exactly as round 2
  949: proposed ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â this piece survives unchanged, now sitting on a sound foundation instead of a broken one).
  950: 
  951: **Cross-tenant envelope** (needed since `DomainEvent.tenantId: string` is non-optional,
  952: `src/shared/contracts/events.ts:24`): continuation events use `tenantId: "SYSTEM"` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a documented
  953: sentinel, precedented by this same file's existing `actor: { type: "SYSTEM" }` shape for
  954: system-originated events (no new concept, reuses an existing "not a real tenant" convention this
  955: codebase already has).
  956: 
  957: ## Required change 3: work-unit enumeration ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â matches today's exact loop shape
  958: 
  959: Round 2 wrongly collapsed to "one message per shard." Corrected: the EventBridge-triggered
  960: invocation reproduces `producer.ts:161-168`'s existing enumeration exactly ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `lookback` (default 15,
  961: `deps.lookbackMinutes ?? 15`, unchanged constant) inclusive minutes ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ `activeGenerations(shardConfig,
  962: now)` (unchanged, handles legacy generations already) ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ that generation's shard partitions
  963: (`gsi3PartitionsForMinute`, unchanged) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â for EACH resulting (generation, shardId, minute) triple,
  964: attempts a lease acquire and, if it wins (fresh or reclaim), sends ONE start message. A triple
  965: whose lease is already `IN_PROGRESS`-unexpired or `COMPLETED` is skipped (no message sent) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â
  966: exactly today's implicit "already done" behavior, now explicit. **Lease key now includes
  967: generation**: `PK: SCAN#<shardFnVersion>#<shardId>#<minuteISO>`, `SK: LEASE` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â collision-free
  968: across reshard generations (round 2's gap, fixed). At `lookback=15` ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ up to 2 concurrent
  969: generations (a reshard transition window) ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ 4 shards = up to 120 (generation,shard,minute) triples
  970: evaluated per tick, but the vast majority are cheap `COMPLETED`-skip reads (already-finished older
  971: minutes) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â only the LATEST 1-2 minutes per (generation,shard) are ever genuinely `IN_PROGRESS`
  972: under normal load, so real concurrent scan work stays bounded near `generations ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ shards` (ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â°Ã‚Â¤8), not
  973: 120 (this bound feeds Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§8's revised capacity numbers).
  974: 
  975: ## Required change 4: message shapes ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â command-envelope for candidates, new system-envelope only for continuation
  976: 
  977: **Claim-candidate messages** (`SQS_REMINDER_CLAIM_CANDIDATE_V1`, NOT outbox-routed ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â no aggregate
  978: transaction backs a raw GSI3 row) genuinely have a `tenantId` (parsed from `GSI3SK` before
  979: publishing) and DO fit the existing `command-envelope.v1.json` shape unmodified: `commandType:
  980: "reminder.claim-candidate.v1"`, `tenantId` (real tenant), `deduplicationKey:
  981: "${tenantId}|${occurrenceId}|${pageOwnerToken}"`, `data: { occurrenceKey: {PK,SK}, entityType,
  982: gsi3sk }`. New schema file `schemas/queues/reminder-claim-candidate.v1.json`:
  983: `"allOf": [{ "$ref": "command-envelope.v1.json" }, { "properties": { "data": { "required":
  984: ["occurrenceKey","entityType","gsi3sk"], "properties": { "entityType": { "enum":
  985: ["ReminderOccurrence","DocumentChasingOccurrence"] }, ... } } } }]` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â same `allOf` pattern as
  986: `reminder-dispatch.v1.json:6-22` (re-read this round, confirmed shape).
  987: 
  988: **Scan-continuation messages** genuinely have no real tenant (cross-shard/tenant coordination) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â
  989: forcing them into `command-envelope.v1.json` (which requires a real `tenantId`) would be a lie, so
  990: a NEW `schemas/queues/system-envelope.v1.json` is added: same shape as `command-envelope.v1.json`
  991: minus the `tenantId` requirement, plus a fixed `"tenantId": { "const": "SYSTEM" }` (kept present,
  992: not dropped, so every queue message in this codebase has the same top-level field set ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â simpler
  993: for any shared tooling that reads `tenantId` generically off an envelope, e.g. log correlation).
  994: `schemas/queues/reminder-scan-continuation.v1.json` uses `allOf: [{"$ref":
  995: "system-envelope.v1.json"}, ...]`, `data: { shardFnVersion, shardId, minute, ownerToken,
  996: lastEvaluatedKey (nullable) }`. Both new schemas get valid+invalid fixtures added to the existing
  997: consolidated `test/contract/schemas.test.ts` (round 2's correction, unchanged).

  999: ## Required change 5: sender-fault candidates ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â terminal, not dropped
 1000: 
 1001: Reversed from round 2: **any `SenderFault: true` entry in a `SendMessageBatch` response fails the
 1002: WHOLE page invocation** (throws after attempting the OTHER entries in that chunk, so
 1003: non-sender-fault entries still get their retry chance first) rather than being silently dropped.
 1004: This means the checkpoint transaction (Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§1-2) never runs for that page, so no continuation is ever
 1005: produced for it ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â the chain is stuck `IN_PROGRESS` until `leaseUntil` expires, at which point the
 1006: NEXT eligible tick's reclaim (Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§3) retries the ENTIRE page from the same `lastEvaluatedKey` (safe,
 1007: `queryGsi3Page` is a pure read). New metric `CandidateSenderFault` (Count, no dimensions) with an
 1008: alarm at >0 over any 5-minute period (fast detection ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a sender fault means a real bug in candidate
 1009: construction, worth paging on immediately rather than waiting for the DLQ-age alarm's 1-hour
 1010: threshold). Retryable (non-sender-fault) entries: the ENTIRE original chunk is retried (not just
 1011: the failed IDs) using `nextAttemptDelayMs` (`outbox.ts:192-197`, reused as-is ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â same backoff
 1012: shape, not reinvented), capped at 3 attempts before the page throws as a transient failure (goes
 1013: through normal SQS-level retry of the scan/continuation message itself, `maxReceiveCount=5`).

 1131: ## Required change 11: reconciliation and claim extraction

 1848: 296:12:## Research declaration (research-protocol.md, E-014)
 1849: 297:13:
 1850: 298:14:**SIM PARCIAL.** The macro-pattern (decouple scan from claim via two queues) is already
 1851: 299:15:externally researched and cited in D-299 (AWS Prescriptive Guidance, Lambda+SQS developer guide,
 1852: 300:16:SQS API reference). What's new at THIS level is a sub-decision AWS has a well-documented but
 1853: 301:17:non-obvious answer for: **SQS visibility timeout sizing relative to Lambda timeout, and its
 1854: 302:18:interaction with `maxReceiveCount`/DLQ redelivery for a handler that holds an idempotency lease**.
 1855: 303:19:This project's own `sqs-worker-queue` module already encodes one specific answer (6x, fixed,
 1856: 304:20:`maxReceiveCount=5`) as a blanket rule for the dispatch case ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¬ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â applying it unmodified to a
 1857: 305:21:lease-holding consumer needs to be checked against AWS's own guidance on visibility timeout vs.
 1858: 306:22:in-flight processing time, because a lease-based state machine changes what "redelivery mid-lease"
 1859: 307:23:means (D-299's own R3ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¾Ã‚Â¢R4 finding). Checklist applied this round, sourced from AWS Lambda Developer
 1860: 308:24:Guide "Using Lambda with Amazon SQS" (event source mapping / partial batch response) and AWS SQS
 1861: 309:25:"Amazon SQS visibility timeout" page (both already cited as sources in D-299, re-read here for the
 1862: 310:26:consumer-timeout-vs-lease-duration angle specifically, no new source needed):
 1863: 311:27:1. Visibility timeout must exceed **worst-case** processing time, not average ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¬ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â for a lease-based
 1864: 312:28:   consumer, worst case includes lease renewal, not just one page's work.
 1865: 313:29:2. `maxReceiveCount` ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â avg processing time bounds how long a poison message cycles before DLQ ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¬ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â
 1866: 314:30:   must be reconciled with lease `leaseUntil` duration so an expired lease and an SQS redelivery

 1869: 317:33:3. Batch size for the scan-continuation queue must stay effectively 1 (see ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§3 below) ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¬ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â AWS's own
 1870: 318:34:   guidance warns partial-batch-failure handling gets materially harder above batch size 1 when
 1871: 319:35:   messages are causally chained (continuation N+1 must not be visible before N's page commits).

 1968: 416:132:

 1970: 418:134:  renew/acquire ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¬ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â bounded work, generous margin over p99). ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¾Ã‚Â¢ scan queue visibility timeout = 180s

 1975: 423:139:- **Lease duration** (`leaseUntil - leaseAcquiredAt`): **90s** ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¬ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â set independently of the Lambda

 1981: 429:145:  SAME message can never arrive before the lease it would contend with has already legitimately
 1982: 430:146:  expired ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¬ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â removing the specific race D-299 R3 found (two live workers believing they both hold
 1983: 431:147:  the lease) by construction, not by luck.
 1984: 432:148:- **`maxReceiveCount=5` (fixed)** on the scan queue means a poison continuation message cycles for
 1985: 433:149:  up to 5ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â180s = 900s (15 min) before DLQ ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¬ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â acceptable, since EventBridge Scheduler fires a new
 1986: 434:150:  tick every 60s regardless, so a stuck shard's lease will be reclaimed by a FRESH tick's message

 1989: 437:153:- **Batch size**: scan queue consumer batch size = **1** (continuation messages are causally

 2102: 550:266:## 7. Migration/rollout
 2103: 551:267:
 2104: 552:268:Big-bang cutover, not staged, for a concrete reason: the scan and claim halves are not
 2105: 553:269:independently useful (a scan queue with no claim consumer just accumulates candidates; a claim

 2107: 555:271:state to stage through, unlike, say, a dual-write migration. Sequencing:

 2110: 558:274:   doesn't publish to it).
 2111: 559:275:3. Deploy the MODIFIED `reminder-producer-handler.ts` (now page-based) in the SAME release as step
 2112: 560:276:   1/2's infra ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¬ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â this is the actual cutover moment; the old monolithic-per-shard loop code path is
 2113: 561:277:   deleted in this same change, not kept behind a flag (D-299 didn't ask for a flag, and a flag
 2114: 562:278:   here would mean maintaining two claim code paths against the same table, doubling the

 2116: 564:280:4. **Occurrences already `SCHEDULED` at cutover**: confirmed safe, with reasoning ÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¢ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…Â¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¬ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â `SCHEDULED`

 2122: 570:286:   lost either way, since `SCHEDULED` occurrences are read fresh from GSI3 every tick regardless of

   1: /**
   2:  * Optimistic concurrency control helper - implementation-blueprint.md #5.2 / M0 deliverable.
   3:  *
   4:  * M0 ships no tables/Lambdas yet (that's M1+), so this module only builds the DynamoDB
   5:  * command *parameters* for OCC-safe writes; it does not depend on @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb
   6:  * so it stays testable without AWS credentials/mocks. M1 wires these builders into the
   7:  * actual DocumentClient calls once tables exist.
   8:  */
   9: 
  10: export interface EntityKey {
  11:   PK: string;
  12:   SK: string;
  13: }
  14: 
  15: export interface VersionedUpdateInput {
  16:   tableName: string;
  17:   key: EntityKey;
  18:   tenantId: string;
  19:   expectedVersion: number;
  20:   /** Additional SET clauses beyond version/updatedAt, e.g. { status: "CANCELLED" }. */
  21:   set: Record<string, unknown>;
  22:   /** Attribute names to REMOVE atomically in the same conditional update - e.g. dropping
  23:    * GSI6PK/GSI6SK when a reconciliation-candidate pointer (M3.5) stops applying. Gap noted
  24:    * since M3 (occ.ts was SET-only, cancelled GSI3 pointers were left orphaned because
  25:    * nothing actively queried them); M3.5 needs REMOVE for real because GSI6 pointers ARE
  26:    * actively queried by reconciliation. */
  27:   remove?: string[];
  28:   now?: string;
  29:   /** Extra ConditionExpression clauses ANDed to the base condition, each with its own
  30:    * caller-supplied names/values (W3-06 purge worker's claim/fence conditions - e.g. checking
  31:    * `legalHold`/`GSI6PK`/`purgeAfter` atomically alongside the version check). Each entry's
  32:    * `expression` is wrapped in its own parentheses before being ANDed in, so callers never need
  33:    * to hand-balance parens against the base condition. Placeholder names/values MUST NOT collide
  34:    * with the base condition's (#version/#tenantId/#updatedAt/:expectedVersion/:tenantId/:one/:now)
  35:    * or with any `set`/`remove` generated key (#set<i>/:set<i>/#rem<j>) - buildVersionedUpdate
  36:    * throws before building an invalid ConditionExpression rather than silently overwriting one
  37:    * caller's placeholder with another's. */
  38:   extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
  39: }
  40: 
  41: export interface DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
  42:   TableName: string;
  43:   Key: EntityKey;
  44:   UpdateExpression: string;
  45:   ConditionExpression: string;
  46:   /** Optional, not `Record<string, string>` with an empty-object default (Wave B2B-14, D-119
  47:    * real finding): DynamoDB's TransactWriteItems rejects an explicitly-empty
  48:    * ExpressionAttributeNames outright (`ValidationException: ExpressionAttributeNames must
  49:    * not be empty`) - the key must be OMITTED, never `{}`, when a caller has nothing to map.
  50:    * `buildVersionedUpdate()` below never hits this (it always maps at least #version/
  51:    * #tenantId/#updatedAt), but a hand-rolled Update (update-organization-settings.ts) can. */
  52:   ExpressionAttributeNames?: Record<string, string>;
  53:   ExpressionAttributeValues: Record<string, unknown>;
  54: }
  55: 
  56: interface ScopeCondition {
  57:   namePlaceholder: string;
  58:   attributeName: string;
  59:   valuePlaceholder: string;
  60:   value: string;
  61: }
  62: 
  63: interface ScopedVersionedUpdateInput {
  64:   tableName: string;
  65:   key: EntityKey;
  66:   expectedVersion: number;
  67:   set: Record<string, unknown>;
  68:   remove?: string[];
  69:   now?: string;
  70:   extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
  71: }
  72: 
  73: /**
  74:  * Private core shared by `buildVersionedUpdate()` (tenant-fenced, every ordinary business
  75:  * entity) and `buildAccountScopedVersionedUpdate()` (D-197 fatia 3/5: WhatsApp `WebhookInbox`,
  76:  * the first entity in this repo with no tenant at all - see
  77:  * `docs/architecture/reviews/whatsapp-channel-scoping/webhook-inbox-purge-scoping/` for the
  78:  * 3-round Claude<->Codex protocol, both final notes >=9.0, that decided this shape). The ONLY
  79:  * difference between the two public builders is which attribute anchors the scope fence
  80:  * (`tenantId` vs `accountId`) - version increment, `updatedAt`, SET/REMOVE generation,
  81:  * `extraConditions` composition and placeholder-collision detection are a single implementation,
  82:  * never duplicated, so the two builders can never drift apart on anything but their fence.
  83:  */
  84: function buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input: ScopedVersionedUpdateInput, scope: ScopeCondition): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
  85:   const now = input.now ?? new Date().toISOString();
  86: 
  87:   const names: Record<string, string> = {
  88:     "#version": "version",
  89:     [scope.namePlaceholder]: scope.attributeName,
  90:     "#updatedAt": "updatedAt",
  91:   };
  92:   const values: Record<string, unknown> = {
  93:     ":expectedVersion": input.expectedVersion,
  94:     [scope.valuePlaceholder]: scope.value,
  95:     ":one": 1,
  96:     ":now": now,
  97:   };
  98: 
  99:   const setClauses = ["#version = #version + :one", "#updatedAt = :now"];
 100:   let i = 0;
 101:   for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(input.set)) {
 102:     const nameKey = `#set${i}`;
 103:     const valueKey = `:set${i}`;
 104:     names[nameKey] = field;
 105:     values[valueKey] = value;
 106:     setClauses.push(`${nameKey} = ${valueKey}`);
 107:     i += 1;
 108:   }
 109: 
 110:   const removeClauses: string[] = [];
 111:   let j = 0;
 112:   for (const field of input.remove ?? []) {
 113:     const nameKey = `#rem${j}`;
 114:     names[nameKey] = field;
 115:     removeClauses.push(nameKey);
 116:     j += 1;
 117:   }
 118: 
 119:   const expression =
 120:     removeClauses.length > 0
 121:       ? `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")} REMOVE ${removeClauses.join(", ")}`
 122:       : `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")}`;
 123: 
 124:   const baseConditionParts = ["attribute_exists(PK)", "attribute_exists(SK)", "#version = :expectedVersion", `${scope.namePlaceholder} = ${scope.valuePlaceholder}`];
 125:   for (const extra of input.extraConditions ?? []) {
 126:     for (const [nameKey, name] of Object.entries(extra.names ?? {})) {
 127:       if (nameKey in names) throw new Error(`extraConditions name placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${nameKey}`);
 128:       names[nameKey] = name;
 129:     }
 130:     for (const [valueKey, value] of Object.entries(extra.values ?? {})) {
 131:       if (valueKey in values) throw new Error(`extraConditions value placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${valueKey}`);
 132:       values[valueKey] = value;
 133:     }
 134:     baseConditionParts.push(`(${extra.expression})`);
 135:   }
 136: 
 137:   return {
 138:     TableName: input.tableName,
 139:     Key: input.key,
 140:     UpdateExpression: expression,
 141:     ConditionExpression: baseConditionParts.join(" AND "),
 142:     ExpressionAttributeNames: names,
 143:     ExpressionAttributeValues: values,
 144:   };
 145: }
 146: 
 147: /**
 148:  * Builds an UpdateItem input enforcing implementation-blueprint.md #5.2's exact
 149:  * ConditionExpression: attribute_exists(PK) AND attribute_exists(SK) AND
 150:  * #version = :expectedVersion AND #tenantId = :tenantId, and increments version atomically.
 151:  * Contractually unchanged by the account-scoped sibling below - same signature, same generated
 152:  * expression, byte-for-byte, for every one of this repo's ~40 existing call sites.
 153:  */
 154: export function buildVersionedUpdate(input: VersionedUpdateInput): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
 155:   return buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input, { namePlaceholder: "#tenantId", attributeName: "tenantId", valuePlaceholder: ":tenantId", value: input.tenantId });
 156: }
 157: 
 158: export interface AccountScopedVersionedUpdateInput extends ScopedVersionedUpdateInput {
 159:   /** External vendor account id (e.g. a WhatsApp Business Account id) - NEVER a tenant id, real
 160:    * or fabricated. Fences the update to the row's own account, same OCC-plus-scope-fence
 161:    * structure as `buildVersionedUpdate()`, for an entity that genuinely has no tenant. */
 162:   accountId: string;
 163: }
 164: 
 165: /**
 166:  * Account-scoped sibling of `buildVersionedUpdate()` (D-197 fatia 3/5) - identical
 167:  * ConditionExpression shape, `#accountId = :accountId` in place of `#tenantId = :tenantId`. Exists
 168:  * for exactly one entity today: WhatsApp `WebhookInbox` (`purgeScope: "ACCOUNT"`, permanently
 169:  * account-owned - see the purge-scoping decision this sibling builder itself depends on). Never
 170:  * use this for an entity that has (or could ever have) a real tenant - `buildVersionedUpdate()`
 171:  * is the only builder any tenant-scoped entity may use.
 172:  */
 173: export function buildAccountScopedVersionedUpdate(input: AccountScopedVersionedUpdateInput): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
 174:   return buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input, { namePlaceholder: "#accountId", attributeName: "accountId", valuePlaceholder: ":accountId", value: input.accountId });
 175: }
 176: 
 177: export interface DynamoPutCommandInput {
 178:   TableName: string;
 179:   Item: Record<string, unknown>;
 180:   ConditionExpression: string;
 181:   ExpressionAttributeNames?: Record<string, string>;
 182:   ExpressionAttributeValues?: Record<string, unknown>;
 183: }
 184: 
 185: /**
 186:  * Builds a PutItem input for first-time creation of a versioned entity, per
 187:  * implementation-blueprint.md #5.2: ConditionExpression attribute_not_exists(PK) AND
 188:  * attribute_not_exists(SK). Caller supplies `item` already containing PK/SK/tenantId/version=1.
 189:  */
 190: export function buildVersionedCreate(tableName: string, item: Record<string, unknown> & EntityKey): DynamoPutCommandInput {
 191:   return {
 192:     TableName: tableName,
 193:     Item: item,
 194:     ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(PK) AND attribute_not_exists(SK)",
 195:   };
 196: }
 197: 
 198: /**
 199:  * Builds a PutItem input that overwrites an existing item gated on a caller-supplied
 200:  * equality condition over specific fields (not a `version` counter) - the pattern
 201:  * `TenantQuotaService`'s `updateConditional`/`putIfAbsent` already use standalone
 202:  * (`identity-store.ts`'s `updateConditional`: full-item PutCommand conditioned on
 203:  * `count`/`resetAt` still matching what was read, not an UpdateItem). Exists so quota's
 204:  * transaction-boundary migration (W3-07 writer inventory) can build the same conditional
 205:  * Put as a `TransactWriteItems` entry via `occ.ts` instead of a hand-written
 206:  * ConditionExpression, per this module's own "never hand-written ConditionExpression"
 207:  * discipline. `names`/`values` follow the same collision-checked merge as
 208:  * `buildVersionedUpdate`'s `extraConditions`.
 209:  */
 210: export function buildConditionalPut(input: {
 211:   tableName: string;
 212:   item: Record<string, unknown> & EntityKey;
 213:   conditionExpression: string;
 214:   names?: Record<string, string>;
 215:   values?: Record<string, unknown>;
 216: }): DynamoPutCommandInput {
 217:   return {
 218:     TableName: input.tableName,
 219:     Item: input.item,
 220:     ConditionExpression: input.conditionExpression,
 221:     ExpressionAttributeNames: input.names,
 222:     ExpressionAttributeValues: input.values,
 223:   };
 224: }
 225: 
 226: /**
 227:  * TransactWriteItems entry shapes - moved here from expiration/ports/expiration-store.ts
 228:  * (2026-08-19, Engineering Maturity Review): that was the only place they were declared,
 229:  * but reminder/ports/reminder-store.ts already re-exported them from there (a cross-module
 230:  * ports->ports dependency), and expiration/domain/audit-event.ts imported them directly,
 231:  * which is a domain->ports boundary violation dependency-cruiser catches but ESLint's
 232:  * text-matching no-restricted-imports rule cannot (it only matches literal specifier
 233:  * substrings, and this codebase's relative imports never contain "modules/"). Reuses the
 234:  * inner Put/Update shapes already defined above instead of re-declaring them a third time.
 235:  */
 236: export interface TransactPutEntry {
 237:   Put: DynamoPutCommandInput;
 238: }
 239: 
 240: export interface TransactUpdateEntry {
 241:   Update: DynamoUpdateCommandInput;
 242: }

docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-88-Lambda timeout; this is a NAMED, bounded wait (not "monitoring, non-blocking" as round 4 wrongly
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-89-called it), stated as a concrete runbook step with a concrete number, not an operator's judgment
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-90-call.
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-91-
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-92-**Epoch fence** (answers Codex's deeper point — a quiesced system can still hold OLD, valid-looking
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-93-messages whose replay is semantically stale): every start/continuation event's `data` gains one
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md:94:more field, `rolloutEpoch` (an integer, incremented each time `SCAN_MODE` flips `LEGACY`→`PAGED`,
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-95-stored as a Lambda environment variable alongside `SCAN_MODE` itself, e.g.
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md:96:`SCAN_MODE_EPOCH="2"`). The scan handler, on receiving ANY message (start or continuation),
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md:97:compares the message's `rolloutEpoch` against its OWN environment's current `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH`; a
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-98-mismatch (message from a PRIOR epoch — i.e., queued before the last rollback/roll-forward cycle) is
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-99-treated as a stale no-op, ack'd and dropped, logged `"stale epoch, dropped"` with a
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-100-dedicated metric (`StaleEpochMessageDropped`, Count) so an operator can see this happening rather
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-101-than have it silently vanish. This makes "leave residual messages queued for a future re-enable"
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-102-actually safe by construction (Codex's exact objection) — a future re-enable bumps the epoch again,
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-103-so anything left over from BEFORE the rollback is automatically invalidated rather than assumed
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-104-valid via idempotency alone. Claim-candidate messages do NOT need this fence (they're not part of
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-105-the lease chain — a stale candidate simply attempts its normal conditional claim, which is either
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-106-still valid, in which case claiming it late is correct behavior no different from claiming it on
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-107-time, or already resolved, in which case the existing not-found/lost-race no-op paths handle it —
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-5-claude-revision.md-108-no new field needed there, kept as-is from round 4).

docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-11-
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-12-**Every** lease-row write that implies "a message should eventually exist" is now one
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-13-`TransactWriteItems` containing the lease write AND an `appendToTransaction` outbox Put, using the
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-14-SAME `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` destination for all of them (a "start" message is simply a
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-15-continuation with `lastEvaluatedKey: undefined` — already true since round 1, now load-bearing:
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-16-the wire shape doesn't distinguish start from continuation, only the outbox-atomicity guarantee
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-17-does, uniformly).
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-18-
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-19-| Transition | Item write | Condition | Outbox entry? |
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-20-|---|---|---|---|
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-21-| **Fresh acquire** (page 1, no prior lease row) | `buildConditionalPut`: `Item: { PK, SK: "LEASE", entityType: "ReminderScanLease", status: "IN_PROGRESS", ownerToken: newToken, leaseUntil: now+200s, lastEvaluatedKey: undefined, pagesProcessed: 0, candidatesPublished: 0, version: 1, purgeAfterTtl: now/1000 + 7*24*3600 }`, `conditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(PK)"` | row must not exist | YES — start message, `lastEvaluatedKey: undefined` |
docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-22-| **Reclaim** (row exists, expired) | Same `buildConditionalPut` shape, `Item.version: 1` reset (a reclaim is a fresh chain, not a continuation of the dead one's counters — `pagesProcessed`/`candidatesPublished` reset to 0, new `ownerToken`), `conditionExpression: "status = :inProgress AND leaseUntil < :now"` (values supplied) | row exists, expired | YES — start message, `lastEvaluatedKey: undefined` (restart from page 1 — the dead chain's `lastEvaluatedKey` is discarded, since `queryGsi3Page` is a pure read and redoing it from the top is simpler and cheap at `limit:200`, and safer than trusting a half-written cursor from a chain that died for an unknown reason) |

docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md-160-again, both at the code-path level AND the message-consumption level (round 3 only had the former).

docs/architecture/decisions-log.md-74-| D-054 | Amendment ao D-053 (Full BFF), a partir de auditoria adversarial independente trazida por Marcelo com 16 pontos técnicos específicos — protocolo Claude↔Codex completo (Rodada A: Claude verifica os 16 pontos contra código real + fontes externas atuais, RFC 9700/RFC 10017 confirmados; docs/architecture/decisions-log.md:98:| D-078 | W3-07 — mesma sessão de D-076/D-077, item 3 do prompt de retomada: mitigação defensiva barata para o risco de admissão parcial em `import-service.ts`'s `reserveImport()`, sem forçar a decisão de produto (unificar quota+idempotency+job-create numa única transação maior, trade-off latência-vs-atomicidade) que D-074/D-075 deixaram deliberadamente para o dono do produto. `idempotency.begin()` e as duas reservas `quota.consume()` (IMPORT_COUNT/IMPORT_BYTES) continuam fora da transação fenceada que cria o `ImportJob` — isso NÃO muda. O que muda: quando a criação fenceada falha (rejeição da fence OU um conflito OCC comum), o `catch` agora libera best-effort o que já tinha sido reservado — `idempotency.abort()` (a mesma primitiva já usada por `renewItem`'s caminho de conflito OCC, "idempotency liveness residual") e `quota.release()` para os dois tipos — antes de relançar o erro original. Toda compensação roda via `Promise.allSettled` (nunca deixa uma falha de compensação mascarar o erro real nem travar a resposta ao chamador). Sem isso: uma rejeição deixava a chave de idempotência presa em `IN_PROGRESS` para sempre (todo retry, mesmo depois do tenant voltar a ACTIVE, batia em `ConcurrentOperationError` permanentemente) e a quota consumida vazava até expirar a janela — com isso, uma rejeição volta o tenant ao estado pré-tentativa (quota liberada, idempotency key livre para nova tentativa), sem alterar o que já era aceito por design para essa classe de risco (uma falha DEPOIS da transação fenceada, ex. entre commit e presign, continua não coberta — fora do escopo desta mitigação). **Achado real de infraestrutura de teste descoberto e corrigido nesta sessão**: `InMemoryImportStore.transactWrite` (o fake usado pelos testes de `ImportService`) só reconhecia a convenção `#version = :expectedVersion`/`#setN`/`:setN` de `buildVersionedUpdate` para condição e aplicação de `Update` — a condição `#status = :expected` de `transitionIdempotencyStatus` (usada por `idempotency.abort()`) nunca era avaliada (sempre "passava" silenciosamente) e o SET correspondente (`#status`/`#requestHash`/`#responseRef`/`#completedAt`, nomes literais, não a convenção `#setN`) nunca era aplicado — ou seja, `abort()` "funcionava" sem erro mas não mudava nada de verdade, mascarando completamente a mitigação nos testes. Generalizado para um parser genérico de `ConditionExpression`/`UpdateExpression` (`splitTopLevelAnd`/`evaluateEqualityClause`/`applyUpdateExpression`) que avalia QUALQUER cláusula de igualdade `#name = :value` e aplica QUALQUER `SET`/`REMOVE` nomeado, não só a convenção `#setN` — acerta tanto o caso antigo quanto o novo sem duplicar lógica. **IMPLEMENTED + UNIT TESTED** (2 testes adversariais novos em `test/unit/import/import-service.test.ts`: rejeição por DELETING libera a quota IMPORT_COUNT/IMPORT_BYTES de volta a 0; rejeição por DELETING aborta o idempotency record, permitindo retry bem-sucedido com a MESMA Idempotency-Key uma vez o tenant voltando a ACTIVE). 1034 testes de backend passando (era 1032), typecheck/lint/check-boundaries/check-docs limpos, zero regressão | Type 1 (nível 3-4, mitigação defensiva mecânica que não altera a fronteira transacional nem o trade-off já identificado como decisão de produto) | N/A — mitigação de menor esforço já sugerida pelo Codex em D-075, não uma nova decisão de arquitetura | N/A | **IMPLEMENTED + UNIT TESTED** — a admissão parcial em si (quota/idempotency fora da transação fenceada) permanece decisão de produto pendente, mas o vazamento residual de uma tentativa REJEITADA (quota presa, idempotency key presa) está fechado | `src/modules/import/application/import-service.ts`, `test/unit/import/import-service.test.ts`, `test/unit/import/in-memory-store.ts` | 2026-08-29 |

Protocolo Claude↔Codex completo, **3 rodadas** (Rodada 1: régua 8,5/design 8,7 — Codex achou 3 imprecisões reais na fundamentação, não na conclusão: alegação normativa excessiva sobre a AWS "proibir" branching, duração "minutos, não horas" não demonstrada pelo `visibility_timeout_seconds = consumer_timeout_seconds * 6` real, e a taxonomia de `retryable` caracterizada como "base sã para política de branching" quando na verdade `toAppError()`'s fallback (`InternalError`, `retryable:false` para qualquer erro não reconhecido) é evidência ATIVA contra isso; Rodada 2 corrigiu as 3 imprecisões sem mudar a conclusão — Claude 9,0/Codex 9,6, gate atingido; Rodada 3 tréplica de fechamento, Claude 9,3). **Pesquisa externa (SIM)**: AWS Lambda Developer Guide, "Handling errors for an SQS event source in Lambda" + "Using Lambda with Amazon SQS" (`docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/`, WebFetch 2026-08-31) — todos os exemplos de referência oficiais (10 linguagens) reportam qualquer exceção capturada como `batchItemFailure` incondicional, nenhum ramifica por tipo/classe de erro; nenhum padrão de classificação de erro para roteamento direto a DLQ é oferecido como recomendação central. **Decisão**: nenhum handler SQS deste sistema passa a ramificar sobre `retryable`. Mecanismo de retry-vs-terminal continua exclusivamente nativo do SQS (`maxReceiveCount=5` uniforme, `infra/modules/sqs-worker-queue/main.tf`, provado por `stack.tftest.hcl`/`sqs_worker_queue.tftest.hcl`) + DLQ redrive — nenhuma chamada SQS explícita nova, nenhum roteamento paralelo. Razão central: assimetria de blast radius — um falso-terminal sob o regime atual não tem efeito extra (mensagem retentada normalmente de qualquer forma); sob um regime de branch-and-terminate, pularia processamento devido de uma mensagem legitimamente retryable. **Classificação de `app-error.ts` auditada e considerada consistente** (nenhuma inconsistência real encontrada nas subclasses existentes — `ExtractionCommitFailedError` com `retryable:true` é a única exceção à regra "validação/regra de negócio = false", e é correta por documentação própria); nenhuma mudança de classificação proposta. **Implementação (documentação apenas, sem mudança de runtime)**: comentários de `AppError`/`isRetryable()` em `src/shared/errors/app-error.ts` reescritos de "pendência" para "decidido, ver D-128"; redação contraditória ("poison message... not retryable" + ainda reportado como batch failure) corrigida em `reminder-dispatch-handler.ts`/`email-delivery-handler.ts` (os 2 handlers lidos linha a linha nesta rodada — demais consumidores SQS do sistema não tocados, decisão é uniforme e independe de detalhe por handler). **Blast radius de errar esta decisão**: baixo — revisitável isoladamente por fila/handler no futuro só sob evidência operacional concreta (saturação, custo material, atraso mensurável), rollback trivial (nenhuma infraestrutura nova para desfazer). | Type 1 (nível 5, política comportamental de retry/DLQ + resíduo de produto sob autoridade ampliada) | 9,3 | 9,6 | **APPROVED** (3 rodadas, gate 9,0 atingido em ambos sem arredondar) — documentação implementada, sem mudança de runtime/infra | `docs/architecture/reviews/appError-retryable-sqs-scoping/` (round-1 a round-3), `src/shared/errors/app-error.ts`, `src/runtime/aws/handlers/{reminder-dispatch-handler,email-delivery-handler}.ts` | 2026-08-31 |

Decisão: manter essa ordem — `idempotencyKey` identifica uma operação lógica, a primeira execução real de um dado key fixa o resultado, uma repetição do mesmo key com `documentType` diferente (mesmo inválido) devolve o snapshot original; C2 formalmente redefinido para cobrir só a primeira execução real. docs/architecture/decisions-log.md-264-| D-233 | **SEC-R2-02 (full-audit-round2, achado convergente independente dos eixos Segurança E Arquitetura) — `deliver.ts` reivindicava o marcador de entrega ANTES de chamar `emailProvider.send()`, sem caminho de volta: uma falha transitória de SES causava perda PERMANENTE e SILENCIOSA da credencial do guest, CORRIGIDO.** Protocolo Claude<->Codex completo (`AGENTS.md` §4, nota cega, `codex exec`, pesquisa real incluída — Codex usou `web search` contra a documentação AWS de Event Source Mapping/DynamoDB Streams retry/partial-batch-response nas rodadas finais): **8 rodadas reais** (7,8 → 8,6 → 8,8 → 8,8 → 8,9 → 8,9 → 8,9 → **9,3/10 final**, convergência única do lado Codex — protocolo de nota cega aplicado ao avaliador externo revisando a proposta evolutiva do Claude a cada rodada; Claude concorda de forma independente com nota final 9,2/10, ambos ≥9,0 sem arredondar). **Mecanismo escolhido**: variante ENXUTA e proporcional do padrão já convergido em `NotificationAttempt`/`email-delivery-workflow.ts` para esta MESMA classe de problema (entrega assíncrona at-least-once com efeito colateral externo não gratuitamente idempotente) — reaproveita o PRINCÍPIO (nunca marcar concluído antes de confirmar; estado intermediário expirável para permitir reentrega se o processo morrer no meio), NUNCA a maquinaria completa de 10 status/OCC (desproporcional: um link de guest é um valor estático, inofensivo de reenviar, ao contrário de um envio pago/customer-facing). `GuestCredentialDeliveryMarkerStore.claim()` (boolean) virou uma máquina de 4 outcomes (`CLAIMED`/`LEASE_ACTIVE`/`ALREADY_DELIVERED`/`PREVIOUSLY_UNCERTAIN`) mais `markDelivered`/`releaseClaim`/`markUncertain`. Reutiliza a taxonomia JÁ EXISTENTE `EmailSendFailureKind` (`CONCLUSIVE_RETRYABLE`/`CONCLUSIVE_TERMINAL`/`AMBIGUOUS`, `email-provider.ts`) para decidir: só `CONCLUSIVE_RETRYABLE` (SES recusou ANTES de aceitar) libera o claim para reenvio automático imediato; `AMBIGUOUS`/`CONCLUSIVE_TERMINAL`/uma falha de `markDelivered` DEPOIS do SES aceitar transicionam para `SEND_UNCERTAIN` — terminal para reenvio automático (nunca duplica um envio possivelmente já aceito), sempre pareado com um alerta (`notifyUncertainDelivery`, fila `guest-credential-delivery-failures` já existente, metadata apenas, nunca o token) que sobrevive à própria falha (se o alerta falhar, a exceção sobe e o Streams reentrega; a reentrega encontra o marker já `SEND_UNCERTAIN` e só re-tenta o alerta, nunca chama SES de novo). Uma lease expirada (`claim()` original com 30s) SEM nenhuma transição observada (crash em qualquer ponto pós-claim, inclusive possivelmente pós-aceite do SES) é reconciliada pela PRÓPRIA `claim()` para `SEND_UNCERTAIN` — nunca um reclaim automático para um novo envio; o único caminho de volta a um claim livre é `releaseClaim()` síncrono, chamado apenas no mesmo processo que observou `CONCLUSIVE_RETRYABLE`. **3 gaps reais de infraestrutura achados durante o protocolo** (nenhum hipotético, todos confirmados contra o Terraform real antes de aceitar a objeção): (1) a role do handler NUNCA teve `PutItem`/`UpdateItem`/`DeleteItem` na tabela dedicada (só `stream_read_policy_json` com ações de leitura) — o `claim()` ORIGINAL já estava potencialmente falhando com `AccessDenied` em produção, mascarado pelo mesmo bug lógico sendo corrigido; nova policy `guest_credential_delivery_marker_write` (`infra/modules/guest-credential-delivery-table/main.tf`), anexada só ao handler. (2) o `filter_criteria` do Event Source Mapping só filtrava `eventName=INSERT`, sem excluir os próprios eventos INSERT/MODIFY do marker (mesma tabela, Streams habilitado) — bug latente pré-existente desde D-228 (o `claim()` original já escrevia um marker), agravado por D-233 escrever/atualizar/deletar o marker com mais frequência; filtro agora escopado a `entityType=GuestCredentialDelivery`. (3) `maximum_retry_attempts=3`/`maximum_record_age_in_seconds=3600` não garantiam atravessar a lease de 30s (retries por contagem podiam se esgotar antes) NEM garantiam que um registro que já esperou quase 1h em backlog não expirasse antes da 1ª tentativa — ambos setados para `-1` (ilimitado, bound real passa a ser a retenção nativa de 24h do próprio DynamoDB Streams). **Novo backstop de observabilidade real** (a justificativa original do Claude — "o alarme de Errors do Lambda dá visibilidade" — era FALSA e foi corrigida durante o protocolo: `ReportBatchItemFailures` faz a invocação retornar normalmente, nunca aparece como `Errors`): alarme `AWS/Lambda:IteratorAge` novo (`guest_credential_delivery_iterator_age`, limiar 5min, `alert_topic` já existente) — detecção em minutos de um registro preso reentregando, muito antes da retenção nativa de 24h descartá-lo silenciosamente. A causa raiz real: `tsconfig.json`'s `include` é `["src", "infra", "test", "scripts"]`, então UMA ÚNICA invocação de `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` compila a árvore INTEIRA — ficando exposta a qualquer fixture que QUALQUER OUTRO PROCESSO tenha em disco naquele momento, inclusive uma invocação `npm test`/`vitest` genuinamente separada (este projeto roda rotineiramente múltiplas sessões/forks Claude/Codex concorrentes contra o mesmo working directory, `AGENTS.md` §1/§4 — exatamente a condição que produz o sintoma). **Reproduzido de verdade** (não só teorizado): dois processos `vitest run` genuinamente separados, lançados ao mesmo tempo, cada um rodando um dos dois arquivos — o `tsc` de `system-mutation-allowlist` citou `TS6053: File '.../src/shared/__tenant_fence_boundary_test_fixtures__/bypass-batch.ts' not found` (a fixture do OUTRO teste, já removida pelo `afterEach` dele antes do `tsc` do primeiro tentar lê-la — exatamente o sintoma original do achado do audit). **Fix**: novo `test/architecture/fixture-lock.ts` — lock exclusivo entre processos via `mkdirSync` atômico num diretório sob `os.tmpdir()` (deliberadamente FORA da árvore do repo, que neste ambiente real é montada via WSL2 DrvFs em `/mnt/c/...` — o lock não depende das garantias mais fracas desse mount), com detecção de lock órfão (>5min) e timeout de aquisição (10min). Ambos os arquivos adquirem o lock em `beforeAll` (cobrindo o ciclo de vida inteiro do arquivo, não um teste isolado) e liberam em `afterAll`; `beforeAll` precisou de timeout explícito de 11min (maior que o padrão de 10s do vitest) já que esperar a suíte INTEIRA do outro arquivo é o comportamento esperado sob contenção real, não uma falha. **Verificação real, não só "passou uma vez"**: 2 rodadas de reprodução com os dois arquivos como processos `vitest` genuinamente separados e concorrentes (não só dois arquivos no mesmo processo) — a 1ª (antes do fix de timeout do hook) expôs o próprio achado original (TS6053 citando fixture do outro teste); a 2ª e 3ª (após o fix), ambas 5/5 em cada arquivo, log de debug temporário confirmando aquisição/liberação mutuamente exclusivas do lock (~2min15s de posse por `system-mutation-allowlist`, depois handoff imediato para `tenant-fence-boundary`); suíte completa de arquitetura via `npm test` normal (single-process) também 5/5 arquivos, 36/36 testes, sem regressão. Codex revisou os fechamentos e apontou 2 refinamentos não-bloqueantes (restituição de slot de upload via reconciliador, não TTL direto; chave composta de webhook `provider+tenant+providerEventId`), ambos incorporados. **Reavaliação final: Claude 9.13 / Codex 9.20 (exato) — ambos ≥9.0, nenhum gate violado.**

71-| D-051 | Achado real no primeiro `terraform apply` de fato do módulo `waf` (M10, D-037/D-045 — nunca antes aplicado contra AWS real, só `terraform plan`/`mock_provider`/`terraform test`, todos verdes): `AssociateWebACL` falhou com `WAFInvalidParameterException` porque **AWS WAFv2 não suporta associação com API Gateway HTTP API (v2)** — só REST API (v1), Application Load Balancer, AppSync, Cognito User Pool, App Runner, Verified Access, Amplify. Este projeto usa exclusivamente HTTP API v2 (`aws_apigatewayv2_api`) — a associação era estruturalmente impossível, não um erro de configuração corrigível. A rota pública `/guest/*` já estava deployada e ativa em `dev` sem WAF (Web ACL órfão, sem associação) até esta correção. Resolvido via protocolo Claude↔Codex (3 rodadas: proposta independente convergente → crítica cruzada sobre escopo exato → tréplica fechando valores): módulo `infra/modules/waf/` **deletado inteiramente** (não só desligado do wiring — reconstruir do zero quando existir CloudFront é mais seguro que reaproveitar uma abstração já comprovadamente inválida); mitigação imediata via throttling nativo do HTTP API (`aws_apigatewayv2_stage.default_route_settings` burst=50/rate=25 para todo o stage, `route_settings` burst=10/rate=5 só para as 2 rotas `/guest/*`, mais restritivo por serem as únicas sem autenticação JWT); CloudFront+WAF registrado como débito técnico **bloqueante antes de tráfego público real de produção** (não antes de continuar em `dev`). Residual explícito aceito: o throttle nativo é por rota/stage, nunca por IP de origem — um único IP hostil ainda consome sozinho toda a cota de 5 req/s da rota guest; isso é o motivo formal de CloudFront+WAF continuar bloqueante | Type 1 (nível 5-6, segurança — supersede parcialmente D-037/D-045, só a parte WAF) | 9,2 | 9,3 | **APPROVED e IMPLEMENTADO/DEPLOYADO EM `main`** (PR #39, mesma sessão que descobriu o achado) | `infra/modules/api-gateway/`, commit `db9c587`+ | 2026-08-23 |

73-| D-053 | Refina D-034/blueprint §4.2/§23.1: "BFF de sessão" restrito a `/session/refresh`/`/session/logout` nunca decidiu como o SPA autenticaria as rotas de recurso existentes, protegidas por JWT authorizer nativo do API Gateway (só valida `Authorization: Bearer`, não lê cookie — `infra/modules/api-gateway/main.tf:47`). 74-| D-054 | Amendment ao D-053 (Full BFF), a partir de auditoria adversarial independente trazida por Marcelo com 16 pontos técnicos específicos — protocolo Claude↔Codex completo (Rodada A: Claude verifica os 16 pontos contra código real + fontes externas atuais, RFC 9700/RFC 10017 confirmados; 85:| D-066 | W3-07 (retomada, Round 3) — avaliação de uma análise arquitetural externa (`reviews/w3-07-tenant-cascade-deletion-design/architectural-analysis-2026-08-28.md`, movido da raiz em 2026-08-29) que propõe abandonar o protocolo "claim + outcome" universal de D-065 em favor de um fence `ACTIVE`-only: `ACTIVE→DELETING` como único linearization point de admissão, abandono deliberado de liveness de negócio pós-`DELETING` (não é requisito real — verificado contra `privacy-lgpd.md`, que exige o oposto: bloqueio imediato), cancelamento/saída terminal em vez de recovery para efeitos externos em voo, quiescence como prova de incapacidade de escrita (não ausência física de mensagens), purge físico versionado (DynamoDB + S3, todas as versões/delete markers) com prova de convergência. Codex Rodada E: admissão transacional fechada arquiteturalmente sob um contrato de concorrência explícito ("`ACTIVE→DELETING` bloqueia novas admissões; operações já admitidas podem terminar" — não "tenant está ACTIVE no momento da chamada"); lanes tipadas fechadas arquiteturalmente (faltam detalhes de enforcement); S3 presigned upload e SES identificados como não fecháveis pelo mesmo truque transacional (capability portátil/hop assíncrono real) — políticas explícitas propostas e parcialmente aceitas, pendente de decisão de produto/jurídica formal sobre a política de SES (bloqueio no ponto de admissão vs. lease/drain); achado novo sobre retry de `StartExecution` não resolvido. **Sessão continuada com autorização explícita do Marcelo para prosseguir até o gate de 9,0 ou até ficar demonstrável que é inatingível.** Rodada F: inventário real (grep contra `src/**`/`infra/`, não suposição) confirmou TTLs de presign reais (600s/900s/600s), timeout máximo real de Lambda (60s), timeouts reais da ASL (`HeartbeatSeconds=120`/`TimeoutSeconds=600`), `StartExecution` já trata `ExecutionAlreadyExists` como no-op idempotente, ponto real de persistência de negócio da extração é `commitOrDiscard` em `run-extraction-validation.ts` (não `completeOcr`), e 4 workers de promoção de upload (`upload-finalizer`/`submission-finalizer`/`malware-result`/`submission-malware-result`) com `transactWrite` próprio. O único precedente real de bloqueio (Jira) se aplica a hard DELETE de usuário, operação mais destrutiva sem equivalente direto neste projeto. **Decisão diverge deliberadamente do mercado** (não por convergência externa, registrado explicitamente como tal) — justificada pela natureza do domínio (rastreamento de prazo/obrigação legal tem custo de item órfão mais alto que um board de tarefas genérico). **Achado interno decisivo**: `assigneeUserId` não tem GSI próprio, mas `GSI1` (`GSI1PK=TENANT#t#ITEMSTATUS#ACTIVE`, `projection_type=ALL`, confirmado por leitura direta de `infra/modules/dynamo-table/main.tf`) já é o índice que o dashboard usa para listar itens ACTIVE de um tenant — encontrar "itens ACTIVE atribuídos ao usuário X" é uma `Query` nesse índice já aprovado + `FilterExpression`, zero GSI novo, zero decisão D-026 nova. `ItemWatch` (sem índice viável, precedente B2B-11 de "remover watcher é sempre seguro") e `RequirementAssignment`/`TrackedSubject` (confirmado por leitura que nenhum dos dois tem um segundo campo de responsável) ficam fora de escopo. **Rodada 1 (Codex 7,0/10 design, 7,2/10 régua contestada, não aprovado)**: síntese da pesquisa Jira imprecisa (citava só o ticket antigo, não a distinção real deactivate-preserva vs. delete-bloqueia); TOCTOU real e não resolvido entre o check via GSI1 (eventualmente consistente, nunca `ConsistentRead` em GSI) e a transação de remoção; checklist original subpesava consistência sob concorrência; capacidade por tenant não fechada. **Rodada 2 (Codex 8,1/10 design, 8,4/10 régua, não aprovado)**: pesquisa Jira corrigida (deactivate preserva, delete bloqueia — fontes `support.atlassian.com/user-management/docs/remove-or-suspend-a-user/` + thread da comunidade, ambas fetch direto); TOCTOU aceito como best-effort explicitamente *bounded* pelo status quo já `APPROVED` em B2B-11 (pior caso nunca pior que o bug que esta proposta corrige) — atomicidade perfeita confirmada inatingível (GSI nunca fortemente consistente, `TransactWriteItems` exige chaves conhecidas antecipadamente, máx. 100 itens); checklist reancorado com critério novo dedicado a consistência (peso 25%, contestado de novo por premiar demais uma garantia fraca); payload do erro limitado a 20 `itemId`s + `totalKnown`/`truncated`; decidido "sem bypass de emergência nesta versão" como default normativo (não mais pendência aberta). **Rodada 3 (Codex 9,2/10 régua, 9,1/10 design, Claude 9,1/10, APROVADO)**: critério de consistência repesado (25%→15%, âncora exige declaração explícita de semântica best-effort + observabilidade via mecanismos JÁ existentes — audit event de remoção + log de cancelamento de notificação de B2B-11 — nunca telemetria nova inventada); contrato de paginação explícito fechando risco real de falso negativo (`Query` pagina a partição `GSI1` `ACTIVE` inteira via `LastEvaluatedKey` até esgotar, nunca usa `Limit` do DynamoDB como truncamento — o cap de 20 vale só para a lista retornada, depois de já contar o total real); precisão de citação (conclusão vem da combinação de 2 fontes, não de uma isolada). **Mecanismo decidido**: precondição bloqueante *best-effort* (nunca atômica) em `RemoveMembershipService.remove()`/`LeaveOrganizationService.leave()`, via porta nova `AssignedActiveItemsLookup` no módulo `organization` (implementação real no composition root, mesma classe de decisão já `APPROVED` de `MemberEligibilityChecker`/B2B-11) — nota de implementação do Codex: o `queryGsi1` já existente em `dynamodb-expiration-store.ts` tem `Limit`+break por `items.length`, não deve ser reaproveitado ingenuamente para este lookup. Erro novo `ResponsibilityReassignmentRequiredError` (`BUSINESS_RULE`, `retryable: false`, mesmo padrão de `LastOwnerError`) com `{targetUserId, itemIds (até 20), totalKnown, truncated}`. `ItemWatch` fora de escopo. Calculado da PRÓPRIA `scheduledAt` da ocorrência + 30 dias, setado UMA VEZ em `reminder-materializer.ts` no momento da materialização — deliberadamente nunca recomputado a partir do `deletedAt` do item/policy pai, porque uma ocorrência é naturalmente limitada pelo seu próprio agendamento independentemente do que acontece depois com o pai (dispensa qualquer worker). **Questão em aberto, sinalizada e não resolvida aqui**: `ReminderOccurrence`s materializadas ANTES desta mudança não têm `purgeAfterTtl` retroativo — nenhum backfill foi implementado nesta sessão (nenhum mecanismo de migração em massa precedente existe neste código para um caso análogo); o volume real de ocorrências pré-existentes ainda distantes de `scheduledAt` é pequeno o bastante para não justificar um script dedicado agora, mas fica nomeado aqui para quem revisitar o assunto. **Infra**: novo módulo Lambda `core_user_data_purge_handler` + role/policy dedicados do EventBridge Scheduler + `aws_scheduler_schedule` diário (`cron(0 5 * * ? *)`, 05:00 UTC, depois de `document-request-recurrence` às 04:30) em `infra/main.tf`, mesmo padrão de `requirement_reindex_handler`/`document_request_recurrence_handler` — sem policy dedicada além da leitura/escrita geral tenant-facing (Scan de base table + GetItem em row tenant-scoped comum, nenhum GSI3/GSI6 envolvido). `scripts/build-lambdas.ts` ganha a entrada `core-user-data-purge-handler`. **G-V3 confirmado ao vivo**: mutação removendo a condição `deletedAt = :deletedAt` do delete (simulando ausência da re-asserção) faria o teste de "restore/undelete durante a corrida" passar mesmo com um restore concorrente — confirmado quebrando deliberadamente essa extraCondition no teste, revertida; Investigado antes de corrigir: `SubmitEvidenceInput` (o tipo de input do guest) é uma interface totalmente separada de `CreateDocumentInput` — nenhum tipo compartilhado, nenhuma coerção estrutural forçando os dois campos a andarem juntos.   27: This closes required change 1 completely: a crash between "lease acquired" and "start message sent"
  28: is now impossible by the same construction that already closed the page-to-page case â€” the
  29: acquire/reclaim Put and the start-message outbox Put commit together or not at all.

  31: ## Required change 2/10: independent stalled-lease detection â€” extends `reminder-reconciliation`, not a new component
  32: 
  33: Codex correctly proved lookback-only rediscovery has a real hole (a lease whose minute ages out of
  34: the 15-minute window before ever being retried). Fix: **lease rows get a GSI6 pointer while
  35: `IN_PROGRESS`**, mirroring the EXACT pattern `reminder-reconciliation.ts` already uses for stuck
  36: `CLAIMED` occurrences (`GSI6PK_WORKSTATE_CLAIMED` today) â€” `GSI6PK: "SCANLEASE#IN_PROGRESS"`,
  37: `GSI6SK: "<leaseUntil-ISO>#<shardFnVersion>#<shardId>#<minuteISO>"` (sortable by expiry, same
  38: "query the oldest-expiring first" shape reconciliation's existing claim-expiry pass already relies
  39: on), written in every acquire/reclaim/checkpoint transaction above (one more `set`/removed on
  40: `COMPLETED`, same transaction, no extra write). **`reminder-reconciliation.ts` gets a genuinely new
  41: third pass** (amending, with reasoning, round 1's "no change" expectation â€” the task explicitly
  42: allows correcting that expectation, and this is the correction): reusing its EXISTING 5-minute
  43: `CLAIMS`-mode schedule (no new EventBridge schedule, no new Lambda), it also queries
  44: `GSI6PK = "SCANLEASE#IN_PROGRESS"` for `GSI6SK < now`, and for each hit, runs the SAME reclaim
  45: transition as a normal reclaim (new `ownerToken`, fresh start-message outbox entry) â€” this is the
 144: ## Required change 8: rollback â€” two-step, mapping-gated, no acknowledge-and-discard
 145: 
 146: Corrected: rollback is now symmetric with the forward rollout's two-apply shape, not a single env
 147: var flip. **Rollback Apply A**: set BOTH the scan queue's and claim queue's event-source-mapping
 148: `enabled = false` (Terraform attribute change, each its own resource, no ordering dependency
 149: between them since both moving to `false` commutes) â€” this stops BOTH consumers from being invoked
 150: at all, so nothing is silently acknowledged-and-discarded (Codex's exact objection: a `LEGACY`-mode
 151: no-op handler still `ack`s and deletes the SQS message; disabling the mapping instead means the
 152: message is never delivered to any handler, sitting safely in the queue). **Observe**: operator (or
 153: a scripted check, not a blocking automated gate for this plan's scope) confirms both queues'
 154: `ApproximateNumberOfMessages` + `ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible` settle near zero OR
 155: accepts they won't (a genuine rollback during an active burst may have real backlog) â€” either way,
 156: proceed only once mapping-disabled state is confirmed applied (Terraform apply success is
 157: sufficient confirmation of THIS step; draining is a monitoring concern, not a blocking gate).
 158: **Rollback Apply B**: flip `SCAN_MODE` back to `LEGACY`. Now old code resumes scanning, and neither
 159: new consumer can claim concurrently with it (mappings disabled) â€” "exactly one mode live" is true
 160: again, both at the code-path level AND the message-consumption level (round 3 only had the former).
 161: **Residual queued messages** (scan/claim) are left in place, inert, until either: an operator
 162: manually purges the queues (runbook note, not automated), or a future forward-roll re-enables the
 163: mappings and they're reprocessed under the SAME idempotency guarantees this whole design provides
 164: (stale-cursor no-ops, conditional claim dedup) â€” so leaving them queued is safe, not just
 165: inert, if rollback is later reversed.

CRITIQUE

1. `leaseUntil >= now` — NOT CLOSED mechanically.

The intended invariant is correct and the named test is appropriate ([round-5-claude-revision.md:8](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:8), [round-5-claude-revision.md:17](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:17)). But the proposed implementation uses `values: { ":now": Date.now() }` ([round-5-claude-revision.md:10](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:10)).

`occ.ts` already reserves `:now` for the ISO `updatedAt` value ([occ.ts:85](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\shared\dynamodb\occ.ts:85), [occ.ts:96](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\shared\dynamodb\occ.ts:96)) and explicitly throws when an `extraConditions` value collides with a reserved placeholder ([occ.ts:130](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\shared\dynamodb\occ.ts:130)). Thus the proposed checkpoint does not reach DynamoDB.

Use a distinct placeholder such as `:leaseNow`. Its value must also use the same representation as persisted `leaseUntil`—apparently an ISO string, not `Date.now()` milliseconds, given the transition table’s `leaseUntil: now+200s`/GSI sort-key design ([round-4-claude-revision.md:21](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-4-claude-revision.md:21), [round-4-claude-revision.md:37](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-4-claude-revision.md:37)).

2. Schemas and envelope routing — PARTIALLY CLOSED, but still materially inconsistent.

Reusing `domain-event-envelope.v1.json` is sound. It permits `"SYSTEM"` because `tenantId` is any nonempty string, supports a system actor, and contains the required aggregate/data structure ([domain-event-envelope.v1.json:8](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\schemas\events\domain-event-envelope.v1.json:8), [domain-event-envelope.v1.json:31](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\schemas\events\domain-event-envelope.v1.json:31), [domain-event-envelope.v1.json:40](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\schemas\events\domain-event-envelope.v1.json:40)). The TypeScript envelope likewise types `tenantId` as `string` ([events.ts:16](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\shared\contracts\events.ts:16), [events.ts:24](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\shared\contracts\events.ts:24)). No invented `system-envelope` is necessary.

The `$ref` fix is also repository-conformant: the real dispatch schema uses `"../queues/command-envelope.v1.json"` ([reminder-dispatch.v1.json:6](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\schemas\queues\reminder-dispatch.v1.json:6)), and pinning `commandType` is required by the existing pattern ([reminder-dispatch.v1.json:9](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\schemas\queues\reminder-dispatch.v1.json:9)).

However:

- The claim that `DispatchOutboxRelay` wraps event data into `SqsCommandEnvelope` is false ([round-5-claude-revision.md:63](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:63)). The relay passes `record.payload` to the destination sender ([relay.ts:91](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\workers\dispatch-outbox-relay\relay.ts:91)), and the generic sender serializes that payload directly ([reminder.ts:140](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\runtime\aws\composition\reminder.ts:140), [reminder.ts:144](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\runtime\aws\composition\reminder.ts:144)). The current reminder-dispatch path works because its event `data` is already the complete `DispatchCommand` ([producer.ts:246](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\workers\reminder-producer\producer.ts:246), [producer.ts:284](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\workers\reminder-producer\producer.ts:284)).

- Consequently, the plan must either put the complete SQS command envelope inside the domain event’s `data`, as the current dispatch producer does, or define a dedicated sender that constructs that envelope. The current proposed event data contains only the inner fields ([round-5-claude-revision.md:48](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:48)).

- `rolloutEpoch` is missing from the event schema’s `required` and `properties` lists ([round-5-claude-revision.md:51](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:51), [round-5-claude-revision.md:52](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:52)), even though the rollback section makes it mandatory on every start/continuation ([round-5-claude-revision.md:92](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:92)). Because `data.additionalProperties` is false, a message carrying the fence would actually fail this schema.

3. Rollback/quiescence and epoch fence — CONCEPTUALLY CLOSED, integration incomplete.

The bounded 90-second wait after disabling both mappings is a real improvement and addresses in-flight invocations, provided the runbook starts that timer only after both mappings have reached `Disabled`, not merely after requesting disablement. AWS documents that `Enabled=false` pauses polling and invocation and exposes transitional `Disabling` versus terminal `Disabled` states. [AWS Lambda CLI reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/lambda/update-event-source-mapping.html)

The epoch comparison at handler entry is coherent for residual scan messages ([round-5-claude-revision.md:94](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:94), [round-5-claude-revision.md:97](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:97)). It does not inherently need to appear in every checkpoint condition: after the handler validates the epoch, the owner-token/cursor/version fences protect the lease, while the disable→`Disabled`→90-second quiescence sequence prevents an invocation from spanning the epoch change.

But the mechanism is not yet executable because:

- The schemas reject/omit `rolloutEpoch`.
- The described relay does not create the claimed queue envelope.
- The plan should explicitly require every producer of a start message—including reconciliation reclaim—to stamp the current epoch.
- The roll-forward runbook must bump/deploy `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH` before re-enabling the mappings, with that ordering stated as a gate.

Claim-candidate messages can reasonably remain unfenced because their consumer revalidates authoritative occurrence state conditionally ([round-5-claude-revision.md:104](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:104)).

4. GSI6 citation and D-299 amendment — CONFIRMED at plan level.

The stale two-role claim is correctly retracted. The handler comment still says two ([reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:4](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\runtime\aws\handlers\reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:4)), while Terraform names four authorized callers ([dynamo-table/main.tf:392](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\infra\modules\dynamo-table\main.tf:392)). Reconciliation already receives the GSI6 policy ([main.tf:298](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\infra\main.tf:298), [main.tf:310](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\infra\main.tf:310)), so no new grant is required.

The revision now explicitly amends D-299, explains why the third reconciliation pass is necessary, and requires the consolidated artifact to record the addendum ([round-5-claude-revision.md:122](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:122), [round-5-claude-revision.md:125](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:125), [round-5-claude-revision.md:130](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:130)). That closes the design-level contradiction; the promised final consolidation/comment correction remains an implementation deliverable.

SCORE: 8.2/10

REQUIRED CHANGES

1. Replace `:now` in the checkpoint extra condition with a non-colliding placeholder such as `:leaseNow`, using the persisted `leaseUntil` representation consistently, on both terminal and nonterminal branches.

2. Resolve the event→queue wire-shape contradiction. Either embed a complete `SqsCommandEnvelope` in domain-event `data`, matching today’s reminder-dispatch pattern, or specify a dedicated sender that constructs it. Provide the complete queue schemas rather than relying only on “mirrors” prose.

3. Add required integer `rolloutEpoch` to both start/continuation event and queue schemas and their fixtures. State that all start emitters, including reconciliation reclaim, stamp it.

4. Make rollback/roll-forward ordering explicit: wait for both mappings to report `Disabled`, then wait 90 seconds, switch mode; on re-enable, bump/deploy the epoch before enabling either mapping.

This round does not yet converge to ≥9.0.

[AWS Lambda CLI reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/lambda/update-event-source-mapping.html)

The epoch comparison at handler entry is coherent for residual scan messages ([round-5-claude-revision.md:94](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:94), [round-5-claude-revision.md:97](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:97)). It does not inherently need to appear in every checkpoint condition: after the handler validates the epoch, the owner-token/cursor/version fences protect the lease, while the disable→`Disabled`→90-second quiescence sequence prevents an invocation from spanning the epoch change.

But the mechanism is not yet executable because:

- The schemas reject/omit `rolloutEpoch`.
- The described relay does not create the claimed queue envelope.
- The plan should explicitly require every producer of a start message—including reconciliation reclaim—to stamp the current epoch.
- The roll-forward runbook must bump/deploy `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH` before re-enabling the mappings, with that ordering stated as a gate.

Claim-candidate messages can reasonably remain unfenced because their consumer revalidates authoritative occurrence state conditionally ([round-5-claude-revision.md:104](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\docs\architecture\reviews\reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping\round-5-claude-revision.md:104)).

The handler comment still says two ([reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:4](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\src\runtime\aws\handlers\reminder-reconciliation-handler.ts:4)), while Terraform names four authorized callers ([dynamo-table/main.tf:392](C:\Users\Usuario\Desktop\projects\expiration-tracker\infra\modules\dynamo-table\main.tf:392)).
